problem_type: license and contribution-policy split between AGPL-only intent and CLA/commercial-authority copy
symptom: The repository presented AGPL-3.0-only in package metadata while requiring a contributor CLA and advertising closed-source commercial licensing across workflows, README, forms, and marketing pages.
direct_cause: A contributor-assistant workflow, a commercial-relicensing CLA document, and duplicated customer-facing copy remained after the product decision changed from dual-track licensing to AGPL-only.
class_root: License policy had no single enforced boundary connecting the package license, contributor workflow, contribution guidance, and commercial inquiry surfaces, so stale policy could reappear in any one of them.
affected_population: External contributors who were asked to sign a CLA before opening a pull request
Users and teams reading README, business inquiry, or marketing copy about delivery options
Maintainers relying on CI to distinguish current AGPL policy from historical commercial plans
entry_points: GitHub contributor workflow and signature ledger
Contributor policy and README license sections
Business inquiry form and generated marketing site
Research and plan documents that describe Nomi's policy

external_sources.purpose: Confirmed the AGPL-3.0 obligations used to describe source availability for conveyed and network-interactive modified versions.

invariants: Nomi's current package and customer-facing policy identify AGPL-3.0-only as the only current license.
No workflow runs contributor-assistant and no code branch requires a signature ledger.
Contributor guidance requires no CLA or signature and points to AGPL contribution terms.
Paid service copy describes AGPL-compliant development, integration, deployment, training, or iteration without promising closed-source Nomi licensing.
generality_proof: The policy is enforced at the workflow, contributor-document, repository-copy, business-form, and marketing-source boundaries. The shared checker scans every workflow for contributor-assistant, while the changed source documents and generated-site static test keep the same AGPL-only/no-signature rule visible across all current entry points.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: State the single current AGPL-only/no-CLA rule and the permitted AGPL-compliant paid service boundary.
Fail closed if a CLA workflow, signature ledger, or missing AGPL/no-signature contributor rule returns.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: The policy test enumerates every YAML workflow and rejects contributor-assistant usage, including this representative CI workflow.

same_class_entry_points.entry_point: For Teams, Contributing, and License sections
same_class_entry_points.evidence: The English README now names AGPL-compliant deployment and explicitly says contributors do not sign a CLA or receive a closed-source Nomi exception.
The form offers AGPL-compliant deployment and no White-label/commercial-license option.

recurrence.reason: The same policy can drift whenever a new workflow, customer-facing surface, generated page, or historical document copies the old dual-track language.
same_class_scan: Searched all GitHub workflows for contributor-assistant and all repository customer-facing sources for CLA, white-label, closed-source, and commercial-license wording.
Checked README.md, README.zh-CN.md, CLA.md, the business inquiry form, marketing/content.mjs, generated marketing pages, research HTML, and plan documents.
Checked package.json license metadata and the existing check:cla-workflow command so the no-CLA policy remains a CI contract rather than a prose-only promise.

prevention.invariant: The repository has no contributor-assistant workflow or main signature ledger, and CLA.md visibly states AGPL-only/no-signature policy.
prevention.failure_mode: The check:cla-workflow command exits nonzero if any workflow restores CLA automation, if a stale main signature ledger appears, or if the contributor policy loses the AGPL/no-signature rule.
prevention.strategy: Keep one executable workflow scan and one contributor-boundary policy document, then test the generated marketing and README surfaces against the same wording so stale policy cannot pass in a sibling entry point.

legacy_paths.rationale: The contributor-assistant workflow and its signature-writing path are obsolete under AGPL-only/no-CLA and are removed rather than left dormant.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: The policy split is caused by repository workflow and documentation drift, not a dependency version or runtime lifecycle.

migration: Existing cla-signatures history is retained as historical evidence but is no longer read by CI or required for contribution. Existing contributors do not need to re-sign; new and future contributions follow AGPL-3.0-only without a signature.
residual_risks: Historical release notes and archived plans may still describe the former dual-track policy; they are retained as history and must not be used as current customer guidance.
AGPL compliance for a particular distribution, dependency combination, trademark use, or network service still requires a case-specific legal review.
